ops.title: Codex generated-handler identity: codex.5 independent artifact PASS
ops.body:
Independent generated-handler identity review

VERDICT: PASS for capt-hook 12.51.0+codex.5 in the requested identity scope. No unresolved new identity regression found. This supersedes the rejection of codex.4 and earlier intermediate verdicts; it does not certify the owner's broader make gate.

Task task_bfb3a16b91f9; dispatch ctx_8b688b6db6e3.
Read-only source targets:
- /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/captain-hook/galeocerdo
- /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/monorepo/codex-monorepo

The reviewer changed no repository source, global configuration, or shared installation, made no commits, and spawned no workers. Probes, package installations, and test snapshots are isolated under /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity. The source owner remains responsible for shipping and broader verification.

Accepted immutable artifact

Wheel: /tmp/codex-port-dist/capt_hook-12.51.0+codex.5-py3-none-any.whl
Wheel SHA256: 4cf56a6436c503c99d1162a2424e52b832be4334fff1d59a4719b6172edf5927
Embedded and reviewed captain_hook/app.py SHA256: 4fabb648994d29b1844050793a31fc1a59a4c3fb52fe65897d3f87088b5c35b7
Independent installations: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity/final-a and final-b.

Each installation used uv pip install --no-deps --target with the exact wheel. Runtime probes used /tmp/codex-port-final-downstream-venv/bin/python with cc-transcript 14.19.0+codex.6. Focused pytest used /tmp/codex-port-final5-capt-test-source/.venv/bin/python, which has that same transcript candidate and the complete test dependencies; PYTHONPATH selected the independent wheel installation and reviewer-owned test snapshot. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 kept tests from writing source bytecode.

Why this design passes

The original on registration recorded fn.__code__.co_filename. A gate calls nudge, whose generated handler lives in the framework library. RegisteredHook._state_identity at captain_hook/types.py:1069#fevp cannot relativize that library path against the project/pack discovery root, so the absolute installation path enters the state key. Two baseline library copies reproduced changed gate/nudge keys in both project layouts, two named packs, and a builtin pack; direct on handlers stayed stable.

The final code captures caller_file at captain_hook/app.py:228#amt5 and uses it only for framework functions whose module belongs to captain_hook.primitives.* or exactly captain_hook.style (app.py:250#ckce and :252#ydnk). Every other handler keeps its definition filename at :254#bxbk. The existing framework_frame helper excludes builtin_packs. No public signature, handler object, hook name, discovery API, state-key algorithm, or global caller-stack behavior changes.

An AST inventory found 25 current imported-on call sites: 19 generated registrations in primitives, one styleguide wrapper, three framework-owned loader callbacks, and two direct builtin decorators. RegisteredHook construction occurs only in app.py's existing hook/on functions. This supports the explicit namespace boundary without adding an internal registration API. Inventory: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity/registration-sites.json; it covers current static call sites, not arbitrary dynamic external plugin code.

The owner's final app.py parses to the same AST as the independently tested isolated design. The final wheel's embedded source matches the reviewed bytes. The source-owner regression fixtures also cover styleguide, direct/imported handlers, both hosts, packs, and builtin attribution.

Independent final results

| --- | --- | --- |

| Native Claude/Codex outputs, on signature, hook names, registration fields, nudge max_fires | PASS: equal to baseline for every matrix case | Same matrix and probe.py/run_matrix.py |

Commands: run_matrix.py final and run_counters.py final with HOOK_REVIEW_PYTHON=/tmp/codex-port-final-downstream-venv/bin/python; pytest tests/test_app.py tests/test_pack_imports.py tests/test_nudge.py tests/test_state.py tests/test_decisions_writer.py tests/test_styleguide.py tests/test_cli.py::TestHooksSubcommand -p no:cacheprovider; pytest tests/test_review_fix.py -k 'resolve_target or real_misfire_complaint' -p no:cacheprovider; staged Python /Users/yasyf/.orca/workspaces/monorepo/codex-monorepo/.capt-hook/tests/test_hosts.py -v. Exact runners and install logs are preserved under /tmp.

The five style failures are TestChangeScoping.test_preexisting_violation_in_untouched_region_suppressed, test_write_reports_whole_file, test_partial_fragment_never_raises, TestDiffRule.test_write_introduces_global, and TestAstGrepRules.test_change_scoping_suppresses_untouched_match. They are visible baseline limitations of this review environment, not a green-suite claim or a reason to weaken assertions. The earlier checkout-only transcript environment also lacked ToolUseBlock.origin; that failure reproduced before and after the patch and the staged dependency environment passed the historical tests. No product fallback was added.

Monorepo preservation

The moved rebase_on_dev_before_pr.py is byte-identical to HEAD:.claude/hooks/rebase_on_dev_before_pr.py and the pre-review candidate. SHA256: 74031c65c3809b9a67067558f6cb234e259b96b8c3aec6730ce3ddd97069081d.

The test file changes only the expected generated gate suffix from 0efbf6949c62 to 84a6d4e48926. The latter independently equals SHA256(rebase_on_dev_before_pr.py)[:12]. Updated test SHA256: ccfa8fed56245d2bdfeae719ecfacd2f3a7c71742b751953adbad376895d0dcd. Both entries in /tmp/codex-port-monorepo-rollout.json match current source bytes. Gate policy was not changed to satisfy the test.

Rejected implementations and preserved evidence

- Unconditional caller attribution changed a normal imported function's source to its registration file. The baseline passed that compatibility assertion; the first WIP failed. Evidence: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-wip.log.
- Codex.4's all-framework predicate rebound loader-owned callbacks to Click decorators.py. An isolated CLI exact-row test passed on baseline and failed on that wheel, printing three extra local framework hooks. A second probe showed an internal max_fires=1 announcement acquiring different keys under different invoking filenames. Evidence: /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-cli-baseline-a.log, cli-wheel-a.log, internal-baseline.log, and internal-wheel.log.
- The exact namespace discriminator closes both regressions in codex.5. Codex.4 remains rejected and its immutable wheel is preserved. The earlier detailed review/design record is /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-rejected-codex4.txt, with durable finding note 30129e9695d76f67dba0eda31396b0d595437ece. Initial PASS messages were explicitly superseded when the CLI regression was found; final acceptance names codex.5 and its exact hash.

One-time state transition

Authored generated hooks move once from the old installation-dependent key to the stable author-relative key. Old per-hook counters are not migrated or read through an alias, so a capped generated hook can fire again after this upgrade within an existing session. Normal user on and framework-owned loader attribution remain unchanged. Subsequent library/project/pack installation moves preserve discovery-stamped generated keys. Ad-hoc registrations without a discovery root retain the existing absolute-path behavior.

No broad make repetition was performed by this reviewer. The coordinator/source owner retain the full-suite gate and the separately reported order-sensitive empty-project-discovery test investigation. ccx vcs diff is recorded in /tmp/codex-port-review-hook-identity-final-source-diff.txt; scoped git diff --check passed. Final source and wheel results were sent directly to owner and coordinator before completion.
